thread:
morgan: Quick Q — where's the canonical place to check TTFT and tokens/sec for hosted inference? Need p50/p95/p99 panels and any trace/log links we should open.

samir: Go to Grafana -> Inference overview dash: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/inf_overview — top-left has TTFT (p50/p95/p99) and tokens/sec by model. There's a small 'Open traces' link on the TTFT panel that opens Tempo traces for slow requests. :mag:

anya: For logs, use Loki: query `{job="inference"} |~ "ttft_ms"` or filter by `model=...`. The panels are driven by these PromQL queries if you want to reproduce.

kevin: PromQL snippets that match the panels: `sum by (model) (rate(model_output_tokens_total[1m]))` for tokens/sec. For TTFT p95: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_ttft_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))`.

morgan: Thanks — yesterday p95 spiked to ~1800ms for gpt-small-hosted. Any recommended alert thresholds while we triage?

anya: Typical starter: alert if p95 > 1500 ms for 5m. Example alert expr: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_ttft_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) > 1500`. Tag with severity=P2, notify platform-oncall and the owning team.

samir: Also check caching/batching signals: look at KV cache hit rate panel and batch size panel. If tokens/sec drops with batch size or cache-hit-rate low, it's a batching/cache problem not infra.

kevin: If you want to dig traces: open a slow trace from the TTFT panel, check spans named `serve.request`, `runtime.kernel`, `queue.wait`. If queue.wait is high that's a batching/backpressure issue.

platform-oncall: Got the ping — I'll check autoscaler, node GPU usage, and recent deploys. Will post findings here in ~15m. :eyes:

morgan: Awesome, thanks everyone — I'll collect the links/snippets and add to the runbook. :memo:
